Sepsis pilot (one med, one surg unit): implement a trigger (NEWS2 ≥5 or nurse concern) → bedside 15‑minute sepsis checklist + EHR sepsis order‑set auto‑populate (labs, blood cultures, IV fluids, empiric antibiotics); roles—bedside RN initiates/checklists, MD/APP confirms/prescribes, pharmacist verifies antibiotics within 60 minutes, unit QI champion monitors; measures (3): process—median time‑to‑antibiotic and % checklists completed within 15 min; outcome—sepsis‑related ICU transfer/in‑hospital mortality (monitored); balancing—ED/ward LOS and fluid‑overload alerts. 
Safety huddle pilot (same units, falls & pressure injuries): replace one nonessential start‑of‑shift task with a 5‑minute safety huddle using a 3‑item risk checklist (falls, skin, mobility) assigning specific mitigations (alarms, toileting plan, heel protectors); roles—charge nurse facilitates, bedside RN commits actions, wound/falls nurse consult twice weekly; measures: process—% shifts with huddle held, % high‑risk patients with prevention bundle; outcome—falls with injury/1,000 pt‑days and hospital‑acquired pressure injuries; balancing—nursing overtime and missed meds. 
High‑risk discharge/follow‑up pilot (medical + surgical): screen at admission/pre‑op for high risk, perform a standardized teach‑back discharge checklist (≤20 min), assign a named contact (discharge navigator RN), auto‑generate plain‑language instructions, and complete a 48–72h follow‑up call by care coordinator; measures: process—% high‑risk with teach‑back + contact assigned, % completed 48–72h calls; outcome—7 & 30‑day readmissions for cohort; balancing—7‑day ED revisits and staff minutes per discharge. 
Scaling and go/no‑go rules: run charts and a weekly dashboard drive PDSA cycles; decision thresholds at 90 days—expand if process adherence ≥70% and a 10–20% improvement signal in primary process/outcome with no adverse balancing trends, adapt if adherence 40–69% or mixed signals, stop if <40% adherence or clear throughput/harm worsening; governance: weekly 30‑minute check‑ins with unit champions, analytics, and QI leadership. 
Protect nursing bandwidth and minimize clicks: each pilot requires a single small trade (e.g., replace one 5–10 minute non‑value task with the huddle/teach‑back), uses EHR defaults/order‑sets to reduce documentation, funds modest supports (approx. 0.1 FTE pharmacist/time‑limited QI nurse champion and four 1‑hour trainings), and assigns executive sponsors plus unit champions to remove barriers.
